newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds sag, long wait until key data.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds sag, long wait until key data.

text.p: *Australian bond futures remained in negative territory going into the lunchtime recess as the market drifted down in the absence of fresh incentives.
*Sustained weakness in local dollar undermining short end.
Australian bond futures remained in negative territory going into the lunchtime recess as the market drifted down in the absence of fresh incentives.

A softer U.S. Treasury market in New York on Monday, which extended into Tokyo trade, provided the mildly bearish backdrop for local bonds which remain devoid of any major data until next week's second quarter inflation and wages data.
"Today's move at the short end was something of a surprise, but the continued weakness of the (Australian) currency isn't helping," one trader said.
The Australian dollar hit a fresh 18-month low of around US$0.7347/52, undermined by the risk of a further easing in monetary policy and subdued commodity prices.

However, debt traders said the currency has yet to get to stage where the possibilty of a rate cut would be ruled out, and although weaker, the September bill contract at today's low of 94.88 is still pointing to a cash rate of 5.12 percent.
Official interest rates currently stand at 5.5 percent.
The immediate focus for the market is U.S. retail sales for June later on Tuesday, which are expected to show a rebound after three consecutive monthly declines.

The local market's softer tone saw it underperform against the U.S., and the long end of the New Zealand curve following the N.Z. CPI which came in line with expectations at up 0.1 percent on the quarter. Spreads to a weaker Canadian market on Monday were little changed.
